d: Atrium of the castle of Montolino: opposite the lake, and beyond the lake, view of the illuminated village.
Valdeburg and Isoletta.
Odonsi cries far away. A brown ship crosses the lake: you can see in it the Stranger covered with a black veil. Many boats chase it.
Mr. Montolino, Osburgo, and other Knights, etc., travel to various parts of the island, which is shivering in Valdeburg.
Montolino and Osburgo.
Interior of the hut where the Foreigner lives. Arturo enters guardingo, etc.
Arturo goes out: he meets in Alaide: she is dressed in black.

Forest near Montolino. I saw in the distance the hut of Alaide. Odonsi from far away sounds of horn and shouts confused with sounds, clue of noisy hunting. The shouts gradually approach, and they sound distinct: they cross the scene various hunters: in the end Osburgo and Chorus.
Valdeburg and Arturo.
As they head towards Alaide's hut, she sees herself coming out of the forest.

A remote place where the Hut of the Foreigner is located, shaded by silvestrous plants. Some cliffs rise from the perspective, at the foot of which is the lake. Arturo, in the south of Osburgo and Hunters. Little by little he begins to darken the sky, and to threaten storm, which in the last scene bursts with extreme violence. Arturo remains long immobile and absorbed in deep thoughts.
Alaide and Valdeburg leave the hut; then Arturo is hidden.
Valdeburg takes Aladis back to the hut: when she has returned, Arturo leaves her hiding place.
He appears from the Alaide hut with a face in his hand.
The inhabitants of the shores of the lake come along with torches. Osburgo, followed by armed men, shows up on the cliff where Alaide is prostrated; he sees it, lifts it from the ground.

Great hall where the court of the Hospitallers gathers, to whose jurisdiction the province is subject: it leads into perspective. At the rise of the curtain, the Judges are all seated on their scans, and in their midst, in higher seat, is the Prior presiding at the court: on the one hand, before the Judges, is Osburgo accompanied by the Terrazzani, who, seduced by him, laid down against Alaide. The hall is surrounded by Guards.
Alaide in the midst of the Guards: it is covered by a great veil: noble is its content, and in the same modest time. The Prior observes some moments, almost struck by some remembrance.
Arturo is rushing into the breathtaking and yearning room.
The door opens at the bottom, and Valdeburg shows up pale, and wrapped in white mantle.
The Prior, Osburgo, Knights and People.
The Prior and the Knights.
Forest as at scene VIII of Act One. Arturo, in Valdeburg.
Isoletta's cabinet in the castle of Montolino. Isoletta alone: it is in a quit dress, and deeply grieved.
Damigelle's choir, it's called.
Atrium that puts at the temple of the Spedalers. The place is occupied by the wedding court. Dames and Knights.
The Count of Montolino, Isoletta and Arturo; in Valdeburg and Alaide.
The Prior with some Knights shows up at the great door.
Arturo, Isoletta, Valdeburgo, and Hidden Alaide.
After a few moments she comes out of the temple Alaide: she is trembling, agitated, and almost outside herself.
Odesi tumulted from the temple and shouting of many voices. From there Arturo comes out in haste, and as if out of himself. Alaide shakes.
The Prior of the Spedalers, Chorus, and People: all flocking. Then Valdeburg.
